    Read the first reason again

    “NOT because it outperformed anything.” A first model has nothing to beat, so criterion 1 passes trivially — and the reason string says it passed trivially. Writing “promoted, beat the champion” about a run with no champion is a lie the model card would then repeat forever.

  8. Into the Aegis adapter, conformance, and the console

    Copy the adapter in. Note the trailing slash on the source — adapter/ copies the contents; adapter would create adapter/adapter/:

    $ rsync -a --delete \
    /path/to/your/adapter/ \
    /Users/yrevash/aegis/backend/src/app/adapter/
    Trap — why not cp -r

    A plain copy overwrites the Python modules but leaves everything you did not replace: the shipped domain's three corpus documents and two skill playbooks. Nothing raises. Retrieval ingests and serves those documents alongside yours, and select_skills may still name the stale playbooks — so the agent cites the wrong domain's policy, on stage. --delete is what prevents that. On Windows the equivalent is robocopy /MIR.

    Run conformance. The --aegis-adapter flag is required; its absence stops with one usage error naming the flag, not with fourteen skips:

    $ (cd /Users/yrevash/aegis && backend/.venv/bin/pytest \
     --pyargs aegis.conformance --aegis-adapter app.adapter -q)
# the reference adapter measures 14 passed

    The fourteen checks, by test name, in test-function order:

    #TestWhat it catches
    1test_every_contract_member_is_presentA piece on disk that nothing imported, so it is not an attribute of the package.
    2test_domain_identity_is_a_usable_topical_railDOMAIN_DESCRIPTION too thin to be a guardrail.
    3test_every_roster_role_has_a_handler_nodeA specialist role with no graph node — it falls back with a log warning, not an exception. The highest-value check in the suite.
    4test_the_roster_default_role_is_declared_and_routableEvery unmatched turn taking the fallback path.
    5test_every_tool_declares_a_risk_tierAn ungated action.
    6test_allowlists_name_registered_tools_and_known_personasA typo in an allowlist. Every typo fails open into silence.
    7test_every_persona_the_adapter_declares_resolvesAnonymous requests 500-ing, or every login raising KeyError.
    8test_the_system_prompt_never_drops_the_platform_floorA rendered prompt missing its platform floor verbatim.
    9test_memory_spec_satisfies_the_memory_contractA missing member that otherwise fails only the first time a conversation is consolidated — i.e. never in a demo.
    10test_skills_directory_holds_at_least_one_playbookSKILLS_DIR pointing nowhere.
    11test_every_playbook_is_reachable_from_select_skillsA playbook the selector can never name.
    12test_ml_spec_resolves_to_the_domain_not_the_fallbackresolve_spec returning FALLBACK_SPEC — four columns named feature_0…feature_3 predicting target.
    13test_seed_corpus_records_carry_identity_and_chunkText in the index nothing can be traced back to.
    14test_no_shipped_domain_vocabulary_survives_outside_the_adapterAny module outside the adapter still naming the shipped domain. The one check that reads the core, not your adapter.

    Quote the test name, never the number. The file groups fourteen tests under eleven section headers, and Aegis's own AGENTS.md calls the vocabulary check “check 11” (its section) while it is the fourteenth test function.

    Re-voice the four console files. This is the step that gets forgotten, and it is visible on screen. web/ is outside the adapter and outside the conformance check, which scans Python only. All four carry shipped-domain literals and will show the old domain's words after an otherwise perfect retarget:

    FileWhat it carries
    web/src/config/personas.tsPersona ids and tool names in its prose. An invented id makes POST /query answer 400 Unknown persona.
    web/src/components/ops/opsShared.tsPROMPT_KEY and tool names inside two prompt strings.
    web/src/components/sim/SimulationView.tsxThe persona id driving the scripted demo.
    web/src/components/ml/MLOpsView.tsxA literal ML feature row — the old domain's column names, hard-coded.

    The real fix is for the API to serve the persona list and the feature spec so the console reads them like everything else. There is no such endpoint yet, and inventing one mid-retarget is not the moment. Re-voice by hand, and say in your report that you did.

    Finally, wire the ML tools — two lines in tools.py, as shown in Part 3's serve card. That is the point at which a planner can ask the agent “how long will ticket 4417 take?” and get a prediction, an interval, and a reason.

Part 6

Synthetic data, and why R² 0.99 is a bug

Generated data can lie in exactly two directions, and both lies produce a number that looks like a result. This part is about the machinery that makes both of them impossible to ship quietly.

6.1  The two failure modes

Say this out loud

Aegis's own reference generator sits at R² ~0.97–0.98 and should not be copied. It uses a flat noise_scale=4.0 against a latent signal that spreads roughly thirty hours. It is present in the code everyone pattern-matches from, it is not a bug in aegis_ml, and it is exactly the failure this whole part exists to prevent. Recorded at ISSUES.md #15, SESSION.md, and reference/README.md.

6.2  The latent function

A LatentModel is a declaration, not a script. It says: the label is this function of these features, sampled around, with this much irreducible spread. Six parts:

PartWhat it contributes
interceptThe baseline value before any feature moves it.
LatentDriverOne feature's contribution: a weight and a shape. Shapes are identity, log1p, sqrt, tanh, square, abs. The first four are monotone — the property that makes a driver's direction explainable in a sentence.
InteractionTwo features whose combination matters beyond their separate effects. This is what makes a linear probe an inadequate learnability test, and why the probe is gradient boosting.
ConfounderA driver that genuinely moves the target and is never emitted as a column. An irreducible ceiling no model can cheat past — which is what real data has.
MissingnessRulePunches holes in a column, conditioned on another column, at a stated rate.
RealismConfigThe declared ceiling and the realism switches: target_r2, target_accuracy, heteroscedastic_feature, label_flip_rate, class_weights.

6.3  The calibrated-sigma formula, and the variance budget

σ = sqrt( var_signal × (1 − target_r²) / target_r² )

Read left to right in words: the noise standard deviation is the square root of the signal's variance, multiplied by the fraction of variance you want to be unexplainable, divided by the fraction you want to be explainable.

Ask for target_r2 = 0.75 and you are asking for one third as much unexplained variance as signal variance, because 0.25/0.75 = 1/3. Ask for 0.98 and you are asking for one fiftieth — a hairline. The formula makes that trade explicit instead of leaving it to a constant somebody typed.

The unexplained budget is then split, not added:

A detail that is easy to get wrong, and was got right

The confounder draw and the noise draw use independent random streams (_STREAM_CONFOUNDER = 1, _STREAM_NOISE = 2). Sharing a stream between them makes them the same vector, which silently doubles the irreducible spread and lands the realised R² well below the calibrated one — with no error anywhere. The distinct values matter more than the values themselves.

6.4  The realism devices, and what each one buys

The module's own list runs to seven. Each one exists because a specific downstream claim would otherwise have nothing behind it.

#DeviceWhat it doesWhat it buys
1Calibrated σ
RealismConfig.target_r2		Sizes the noise from the signal's own variance.The achievable ceiling is a declared property that can be checked afterwards, rather than an accident of hand-typed constants.
2Unobserved confounders
Confounder		Drivers that genuinely move the target and are never emitted as columns.An irreducible ceiling no model can cheat past — which is what real data has. It also answers the reviewer's question “is the interval wide because the model is bad, or because the world is uncertain?”
3Heteroscedastic noise
heteroscedastic_feature		Makes the noise wider in some regions of one feature. Measured at 1.48× spread between the top and bottom quartiles of transit_hours.An adaptive conformal interval has an honest reason to breathe. Without it, every interval is the same width and the uncertainty story is decorative.
4MAR missingness
MissingnessRule		Punches holes conditioned on another column — ~4% of sensor_gap_minutes, on economy lanes. Measured at 4.23%.The spine's median/mode imputation and its MLExplainResponse.imputed_features field have something real to report. It is also what forces linear members into an imputing pipeline — see §6.6.
5Genuinely irrelevant features
default_latent_model		Leaves some declared features with no driver at all.A model that correctly assigns them near-zero SHAP is a far better demonstration than one where every column is load-bearing. Measured at 1.7% and 1.5% of total attribution.
6Interactions and non-linear shapes
Interaction, tanh, log1p		One interaction term plus saturating and compressive shapes.The problem is not linearly separable, so tree ensembles have a reason to exist — and a linear probe would give a false negative, which is why the learnability probe is gradient boosting.
7Class imbalance and boundary label noise
class_weights, label_flip_rate		Balance away from a tidy 50/50 — measured at 28/72 — plus ~3% of labels flipped near the decision boundary.Corruption where real measurement error actually lives. And it forces the majority-class guard: a 72/28 target hands a constant predictor 0.72 accuracy for free.

Some documents in this repository refer to “the five realism devices”. The module docstring of src/aegis_ml/data/latent.py and reference/README.md both enumerate seven, which is what is listed above.

6.5  The two-directional learnability guard

Two bounds, and they are deliberately not symmetric in how hard they fail.

A real defect, worth knowing

Those two scales are confusable, and RUN_SUMMARY.md confuses them: it prints [0.15, 0.95] — the learnability guard bounds — under the heading “realism band”, while the console correctly prints [0.45, 0.80] from realism_band_for. Open issue #21 in ISSUES.md. The charts and the console are right; that one Markdown label is wrong.

What the guard measures, exactly

AspectDetail
The probeHistGradientBoostingRegressor/Classifier, max_iter=200, learning_rate=0.1. Chosen because it is the cheapest estimator that can represent what the real spine represents — and because it consumes NaN natively, which matters once the missingness rules have done their work.
The split25% held out, stratified for classification.
Minimum rowsMIN_LEARNABILITY_ROWS = 60. Below that, InsufficientLabelsError — a score from twelve rows is a coin flip dressed as evidence.
Constant targetRefused outright. Every metric on a constant target is meaningless: accuracy reads 1.0 and R² reads 0.0. This is the same condition python -m app.ml reports as distinct=False.
Majority-class guardFor classification the floor is raised to majority_share + 0.02 whenever that is the higher bar. A 95/5 binary target hands a constant predictor 0.95 accuracy, which sails past the configured floor of 0.55 while learning precisely nothing.

Measured evidence that the guard works, both ways: a noise target raises LabelNotLearnableError; a deterministic target scores R² 0.994 and is flagged suspiciously_easy. Both recorded in ISSUES.md's “What IS verified” table.

6.6  Missingness has a second consequence

The ~4% missing-at-random holes are not only realism decoration. They decide what may be promoted.

XGBoost and HistGradientBoosting route a NaN down a learned default branch. Scikit-learn's linear models have no such path — RidgeCV.predict raises ValueError: Input contains NaN. A linear member marked portable without imputation would train, score, promote, and then fail on the first live request whose payload happened to omit a field.

So every linear member is wrapped:

Pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="median") → StandardScaler() → estimator)

The median, not the mean, matching aegis.ml.model.TrustworthyModel.feature_medians — so a value imputed during the search and a value imputed at request time are the same value. And the scaling is free with respect to attribution: an affine per-column transform leaves coef_j · (x_j − E[x_j]) unchanged, so the SHAP values still name the caller's own columns.

6.7  When to use SDV instead

Everything above assumes you have no real data and are generating it from a declared function. There is a second path for when you have some.

Use…When…Because…
The procedural + latent generator
data.latent + generator.py		 You have no historical data at all — the normal case for a new deployment. You control the ground truth. You know the analytic ceiling, you know which features are irrelevant, you know exactly how much of the target is irreducible — and every one of those becomes a number a reviewer can check.
SDV
data.synth, aegis-ml synth		 You have a real CSV and want ten times more rows that look like it. SDV learns the joint distribution of the real data and samples from it. You get realistic marginals and correlations for free — but you inherit whatever relationship the real data has, including its leakage, and you do not know the analytic ceiling.
 
$ aegis-ml synth --data real_tickets.csv --out more_tickets.parquet \
    --rows 12000 --problem problem.json --model <synthesizer>
Stated honestly

data/synth.py is recorded in ISSUES.md #6 as the one module in the package with no execution evidence behind it — the signatures are plausible but unproven, and the fix listed is to run it against .venv-ml on a real frame. SDV 1.38.1 is installed in the trainer venv. Treat this path as untested until that is done.

Either way, the learnability guard runs afterwards. SDV output is not exempt — a synthesizer fitted to data whose label was already noise will faithfully reproduce noise.

Part 7

Evaluation, uncertainty and the gate

What the numbers mean, how they are produced, and the five checks that stand between a number and a model going into service. The recurring idea: an aggregate score is not evidence on its own.

7.1  Conformal prediction, in plain words

A normal model gives you one number. “This repair will take 8.4 hours.” That is almost never what a planner needs, because the honest answer is a range and a confidence.

Conformal prediction turns the one number into a range with a guarantee you can check. The method is genuinely simple:

The rule stated once, applied everywhere

Requested and measured are always two numbers. They appear as two fields on TrainResult, two columns in aegis-ml registry, two rows on the model card, two entries in the gate's metrics. They are never merged and never rounded together, because they answer different questions: what did we promise? and what did we deliver?

And empirical_coverage is float | None. A run that did not measure it records None. Unmeasured is not the same as met.

7.2  Metrics, folds, calibration and slices

Metrics carry their direction

HIGHER_IS_BETTER is a registry mapping each metric name to whether larger is better. Nothing in aegis_ml writes a bare > to compare two scores; it asks the registry. An unrankable metric fails the gate rather than being guessed at — the reason string says so: “Nothing here will guess whether larger is better — guessing promotes the worse model with a straight face.”

Words defined
R² (r-squared)
For a number-predicting model: the fraction of the target's variation the model explains. 1.0 is perfect, 0.0 is no better than always guessing the average, and it can go negative if the model is worse than that.
RMSE
Root mean squared error — the typical size of a miss, in the target's own units. Lower is better.
accuracy
For a label-predicting model: the fraction it got right. Beware: on an imbalanced problem, a model that always says “no” can score highly.
cross-validation (CV)
Splitting the data several ways and scoring each split, so you see whether the score is stable or whether one lucky split flattered it.
calibration
Whether a stated confidence means what it says. If a model says “70% sure” a hundred times, roughly seventy of those should be right.
slice
A subset of the rows defined by one feature's value — all the multi_leg routes, all the rows in the top quartile of transit time.

Cross-validation that refuses to average away what you were testing for

cv.cross_validate reports the standard deviation next to the mean, because a mean of 0.72 across folds of 0.71, 0.72, 0.73 and a mean of 0.72 across folds of 0.45, 0.68, 0.95 support completely different conclusions. resolve_strategy picks the split scheme, and TemporalShuffleError raises rather than shuffling a series it was asked not to.

Slices — the aggregate's blind spot

slice_report sweeps every level of every categorical feature and every quartile of every numeric one. A segment too small to score is recorded as a SkippedSlice with a reason, not dropped — because a dropped segment and a segment that scored fine look identical in a table of what remains.

7.3  The measured example that makes the case

This is the single most useful number in the whole repository for explaining why the design is what it is.

91.4%marginal coverage measured, against 90% requested. looks fine
82.9%route_class = multi_leg, over 76 rows. below the 85% floor
5 of 20segments fall below the requested level

Read those together. The headline says the model delivers slightly more coverage than promised — 91.4% against 90%. Anyone stopping there ships it.

Break it down by segment and one route class is covered only 82.9% of the time. For a planner routing a multi-leg shipment, the interval this model gives them is wrong more than one time in six, while the report says one time in ten. The average is not wrong; it is simply incapable of showing this. The collapsed segment contributes only its own 76 rows out of 407, so its failure moves the headline by very little.

This is why the gate compares the worst slice, not the mean

Gate criterion 4 takes the challenger's worst segment and compares it against the champion's worst segment, with a default tolerance of 0.0 — no regression permitted at all. A model that improves on average while collapsing on one region is a regression for everyone in that region, and the aggregate score is precisely the instrument that cannot see it.

7.4  The gate, as five sequential checks

7.5  Two configurations that change the meaning, and say so

SettingWhat it does — and what the record then says
require_empirical_coverage=False Criterion 2 passes with no measurement — but the reason string reads “PASS coverage_meets_request (WAIVED)… The interval this model serves is UNVERIFIED.” The waiver is recorded, in capitals, in the artifact.
require_contracts=False Criterion 3 is recorded as SKIPPED and NOT passed — checks["contracts_pass"] is still present and still False. A disabled check and a passed check must never look the same in the decision record.

7.6  What the gate does not do

Worth stating, so the guarantee is not over-read:

  • It does not test the model on new data. It compares numbers that were already measured during train_flow. If the held-out split was compromised, the gate inherits that. This is why recover_split verifies the split by re-scoring — see Part 3's report card.
  • It does not check the model is fast, small, or licensable. The TabPFN licence notice travels in Recipe.notes and on the card, but no criterion enforces it.
  • It does not stop serving. A drift verdict of block blocks the next promotion. The currently served model keeps serving, flagged.
  • It cannot see a problem nobody measured. Criteria 2 and 4 fail closed on missing measurements precisely because of this — that is the mitigation, not a claim that the gap cannot exist.
Part 8

Improvements

Findings and recommended changes, compiled separately from a full review of the codebase against its own documentation.

An independent audit of the package, done by reading the source and reproducing each finding rather than by reading its documentation. Row 1 was fixed during the audit; everything else is open. Effort: S under an hour, M a few hours, L a day or more.

The shape of the residual weakness. The controls themselves are sound. The gaps are in the seams between them, and they all have one shape: a control that did not run is handed to the next stage as an empty list, a None, or a default — and the next stage reads that as “ran, and was clean.” The promotion gate did this with the leakage audit (row 1, now fixed); the search cache does it with a key that omits the split fractions; hpo.tune does it with a resumed Optuna study.

26Docs vs codeMeasured against the tree: README.md:127 and SESSION.md:116 say 314 tests (actual 323); README.md:132 and ISSUES.md:279 say 14 reviewed opt-outs (actual 17); the no-mocks audit reports 73 source files against README's 59–64. card.json is in store.STANDARD_ARTIFACTS (store.py:80) and mirrored at mlflow_mirror.py:48, and no writer for it exists anywhere. Every aegis_ml.* symbol quoted in the docs does resolve — the earlier drift rounds held.Re-derive the three counts from pytest --collect-only, scripts/audit_no_mocks.py and the audit's own file count, in one pass over README.md / SESSION.md / ISSUES.md. Either write card.json from explain/card.py (it is the machine-readable form an agent would consume, and the only one missing) or drop it from STANDARD_ARTIFACTS.ISSUES #16 criticises Aegis's own repo for exactly this — self-reported counts that disagree with each other — and instructs "record what you actually get". The counts are the cheapest thing in the repo to keep honest, and they are the first thing a reader checks the rest against.S

8.1  Discrepancies found while writing this handbook

Each of these was found by comparing a document against the source it describes, or by running the code. None is a bug in behaviour; all are places where a reader would be misinformed.

#WhereWhat disagrees
1pipelines/flows.py docstring Opens with “Six flows” and then lists seven, with forecast_flow and full_flow sharing a bullet. Verified by import: there are seven @flow-decorated functions. README.md names only four.
2Test count pytest --collect-only -q reports 323 collected in this checkout. ISSUES.md:289 says 323 passed; ISSUES.md:51, SESSION.md:116 and README.md all say 314. Bare-checkout figures also disagree: 306+3 skipped vs 311+3 skipped.
3README.md:307 Describes PORTABLE_KINDS as “an explicit allowlist of tree learners”. It now holds 21 kinds including 11 linear ones. The prose predates the explainer-dispatch fix.
4README.md:82 leaderboard prose Says ridge_reference (0.746) was refused and flaml_xgb_limitdepth (0.7379) promoted. That is the pre-fix behaviour; ISSUES.md:163 records that a fresh run now promotes ridge_reference at 0.7460. Both are true of different runs, but the README does not say which.
5NannyML estimate estimated_rmse given as 2.07 [1.71, 2.44] in ISSUES.md, RESOLUTION.md and README.md, but ≈6.6 in SESSION.md:125. The artifact inspected for this handbook records 8.19. Three different runs, no run id attached to two of them.
6RUN_SUMMARY.md Prints [0.15, 0.95] — the learnability guard bounds — under the heading “realism band”, while the console correctly prints [0.45, 0.80]. Already open as ISSUES.md #21.
7registry.STANDARD_ARTIFACTS Lists card.json, which no flow writes. Already recorded in SESSION.md.
8Realism device count Some documents say “five realism devices”; data/latent.py's docstring and reference/README.md both enumerate seven.
9Figure count report.PLOT_FILES declares ten figure slots and report.plots exports twelve functions, while every run produces nine PNGs — forecast is honestly omitted because aegis[forecast] is not installed. All three numbers are correct about different things, and nothing says so.
10Issue-ledger status ISSUES.md:6 says “14 of 23 fixed”; ISSUES.md:9, SESSION.md:166 and README.md:317 all still say “10 of 16 fixed”.
11Analytic ceiling RESOLUTION.md:170 states the data's analytic ceiling as 0.65; README.md and reference/README.md state 0.74. The run artifacts support 0.74.
12Audit / module counts “14 reviewed opt-outs” vs “there are 15”; “59 modules” (ruff) vs “52/52 imports” vs “64 source files” (no-mocks audit). Each counts a different set; none says which.

Appendix

Command reference, file map, glossary

Reference material. Every command and flag below was read from aegis-ml <command> --help in this checkout, not from documentation.

A  The command line

Sixteen commands. Install with uv pip install --python .venv -e '.[dev]'; the entry point is aegis_ml.cli:app.

CommandFlagsWhat it does (from its own help text)
doctor --problem --domain-id --strict/--no-strict Print the environment, the tiers, the paths and the realism band; exit non-zero if broken. Exit code 0 means the morning can proceed.
init --domain-id* --target --task --unit --out --templates --force/--no-force Write an MLProblem scaffold, and optionally copy the adapter templates. Two separate outputs; --force is needed to overwrite.
contract --data* --problem --adapter Validate a frame against its contract, scan for leakage, and prove the label is learnable.
synth --data* --out* --rows --model --problem --adapter Fit SDV on a real frame and sample more rows from it — the “make 10× more” path.
train --problem --adapter --data --tier --time-budget --seed --trainer-venv/--no-trainer-venv --hpo/--no-hpo --force/--no-force --resume-from --full/--no-full Search, tune, fit, measure and register a model — every number from a real fit.
eval --run-id* --data --allow-in-sample/--no-allow-in-sample Re-score a registered run on data it has never seen. In-sample results are labelled IN-SAMPLE.
promote --run-id* --force/--no-force Judge a challenger against the champion and replace the served artifact if it wins.
rollback --domain-id* Restore the previously promoted artifact for a domain.
drift --run-id* --data* Measure drift against a run's reference frame and estimate performance without labels.
forecast --data* --label* --ts-column --value-column --horizon --freq --level --unit --out --ml-candidates/--no-ml-candidates Forecast a series and report the coverage the band actually achieved.
card --run-id* --format --out Print or write a run's model card.
export --run-id* --out --validate/--no-validate Export a run's fitted model to ONNX and validate the round-trip.
visuals --run-id --all --domain-id --shap-samples --open (Re)build a run's visual bundle: registry_store/runs/<run_id>/visuals/.
registry --domain-id --limit (default 20) --json List registered runs, newest first, with both coverage numbers.
serve --host (127.0.0.1) --port (8099) --prefix (/ml) --reload/--no-reload Serve the ML router standalone, for the console or a quick look at the registry.
dashboard --host --port (8000) --mlflow-port --optuna-port --no-browser --no-mlflow --no-optuna --backfill-mlflow/--no-backfill-mlflow Bring up the hub, the MLflow UI and Optuna Dashboard, and open a browser.

* = required. Flags shown as --x/--no-x are booleans with an explicit off switch.

B  Settings

Every one is an environment variable prefixed AEGIS_ML_ — so promote_min_gain is AEGIS_ML_PROMOTE_MIN_GAIN. Defaults from src/aegis_ml/settings.py; five TOML files under config/ also feed them.

SettingDefaultGoverns
aegis_root../aegisThe Aegis checkout; the served artifact path derives from it.
registry_dir./registry_storeThe source of truth.
trainer_venv./.venv-mlWhere the strong tiers live.
enable_flaml / autogluon / tabpfntruePolicy switches. A disabled tier reports a policy reason, distinct from an uninstalled one.
enable_mlflow / prefectfalseOptional mirrors and orchestration. Off by default, deliberately.
automl_time_budget300 sSearch wall clock.
hpo_trials / hpo_timeout60 / 600 sOptuna refinement.
random_seed7Determinism.
requested_coverage0.90The conformal level asked for.
coverage_tolerance0.05Gate criterion 2's allowance — sampling error, not slack.
promote_min_gain0.005Gate criterion 1's margin.
learnable_r2_floor0.15Below this, LabelNotLearnableError.
learnable_accuracy_floor0.55Raised to majority share + 0.02 when that is higher.
realism_r2_band(0.45, 0.80)Where a credible frame lands.
realism_accuracy_band(0.62, 0.92)Same, for classification.
suspiciously_easy_r20.95Above this is a bug report, not a result.
suspiciously_easy_accuracy0.98Same, for classification.
leakage_threshold0.98A single feature scoring above this is flagged.
drift_share_warn / block0.20 / 0.40Share of features drifted.
postgres_dsnnoneOptional relational mirror.

D  Glossary

Every technical term used in this handbook, in one place.

TermPlain meaning
accuracyFraction of labels a classifier got right. Misleading on imbalanced data.
adapterThe ten-piece Python package holding all the business knowledge. The only thing that changes between two Aegis deployments.
agentAn LLM-driven program that can decide to call tools rather than only produce text.
AutoMLAutomatic model selection — software that tries many models and configurations for you.
calibration setRows held out from training and from testing, used only to measure how wrong the model typically is, so the interval width can be set from evidence.
champion / challengerThe model currently serving, and a new one asking to replace it.
confounderSomething that genuinely affects the answer but is not in the data. Its effect is irreducible — no model can recover it.
conformal predictionTurning a point prediction into a range whose coverage can be measured rather than assumed.
conformanceAegis's fourteen-test suite checking a domain adapter is structurally correct.
coverageHow often the true value falls inside the predicted range. Always two numbers: requested and measured.
cross-validationSplitting the data several ways and scoring each, to see whether a score is stable.
digest (SHA-256)A short fingerprint of a file or table. Two identical digests mean identical content.
driftIncoming data has changed shape since training.
ensembleSeveral models whose predictions are averaged.
estimatorOne model object with .fit() and .predict().
featureOne input column.
gateThe five checks that must all pass before a model replaces the served one.
held-out / test splitRows the model never saw. The only rows a quotable score may come from.
heteroscedasticThe noise is bigger in some regions than others. Real data usually is.
HPOHyperparameter optimisation — tuning a chosen model's settings.
imputationFilling a missing value. Here: with the training median, so the same gap gets the same fill at training and at request time.
joblibPython's way of saving a live object to a file. Only reliable when both sides share library versions.
latent functionThe declared true relationship a synthetic generator computes labels from, before noise.
leakageA feature that would not really be known at prediction time, usually because it is a consequence of the answer.
learnabilityWhether the label is actually a recoverable function of the columns. Provable in seconds.
MAR missingnessMissing At Random — values are absent in a pattern that depends on another column, not on the missing value itself.
one-hot encodingTurning a categorical column into one 0/1 column per level.
ONNXA portable model file format other runtimes can score. Point predictions only — no interval, no explanation.
OptunaThe hyperparameter search library used here, with its study persisted to SQLite so a search resumes.
panderaThe library that turns a spec into a runtime schema check on a DataFrame.
ParquetA compact, typed table file format. Preserves dtypes; CSV does not.
partial dependenceA curve showing how the prediction moves as one feature is swept across its range.
personaA kind of user, with its own data scope, tool allowlist and system prompt.
portable (recipe)Rebuildable in the serving environment. Only 21 estimator kinds qualify.
promotionReplacing the served .joblib file. Atomic, gated, reversible.
pydanticThe library that makes a Python object validate its own fields.
quantileThe value below which a given fraction of a sorted list falls. The 90th percentile is the 0.9 quantile.
R²Fraction of the target's variation the model explains. 1.0 perfect, 0.0 no better than the average.
recipeThe small JSON document describing a model — class names and constructor arguments — that crosses between the two environments.
reference frameThe training data, frozen at training time. Drift is always measured against this file.
registryThe directory tree recording every run and which model is serving.
RMSETypical size of a miss, in the target's units. Lower is better.
SDVSynthetic Data Vault — learns the joint distribution of real data and samples more of it.
SHAPPer-feature, per-prediction attribution that sums exactly to the gap between this prediction and the average one.
sliceA subset of rows defined by one feature's value or quartile.
spineAegis's own ML component — the fitted ensemble, its interval, and its explanation.
stratified splitA split that preserves the class balance in every part.
targetThe column being predicted.
tierOne family of model search: baseline, flaml, autogluon, tabpfn.
toolOne named function the agent may call, typed and risk-tiered.
venvAn isolated folder with its own Python and its own library versions.
